subject: botany_2
question_text: Explain briefly the various processes of recombinant DNA technology.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.14, printed question 3. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Three slips corrected on this card: the guide writes "cellulose" for the enzyme CELLULASE (cellulose is what the enzyme digests), "powered detergents" for POWDERED, and "resoluting enzyme digestion" for RESTRICTION enzyme digestion.

insider_note: Eight steps, eight marks — one mark per step, so the safest structure is eight numbered headings with two or three lines under each. Never merge two steps to save time; you lose a whole mark to save four lines.

steps.label: Isolation of DNA
steps.margin_note: Name all three wall enzymes, both cleaning enzymes, ethanol and spooling. This step alone can be a full mark if the enzymes are right.
lines: 1. ISOLATION OF DNA
The DNA is enclosed by membranes and surrounded
by other cell contents, so it must be freed.
The cell wall is digested by enzymes:
LYSOZYME for bacteria, CELLULASE for plant
cells, CHITINASE for fungi.
RNA is removed by RIBONUCLEASE and protein by
PROTEASE.
Adding chilled ETHANOL precipitates the DNA as
fine threads, which are collected by SPOOLING.
steps.why: Each enzyme is chosen for the wall it has to digest, which is why the three organisms need three different ones.
common_mistakes: Writing 'cellulose' as the enzyme. CELLULOSE is the wall material; CELLULASE is the enzyme. The guide misprints this.
Naming one wall-digesting enzyme. Lysozyme, cellulase and chitinase are all expected.
Leaving out spooling. It is the named step that collects the DNA.
steps.memory_tip: One enzyme per wall: lysozyme, cellulase, chitinase.

steps.label: Fragmentation of DNA
steps.margin_note: Name the enzyme class, name the process, and say why the SAME enzyme is used.
lines: 2. FRAGMENTATION OF DNA
The purified DNA is cut into fragments by
RESTRICTION ENZYMES.
This process is called RESTRICTION ENZYME
DIGESTION.
The vector and the source DNA are cut with the
SAME enzyme, so their sticky ends match.
steps.why: Cutting both molecules with the same enzyme produces complementary sticky ends, which is the only reason ligase can later join them.
common_mistakes: Using different enzymes on the two DNAs. They must be cut with the SAME one.
Writing 'resoluting enzyme digestion'. It is RESTRICTION enzyme digestion.

steps.label: Isolating the desired fragment
steps.margin_note: The technique, the direction and why, and the recovery step.
lines: 3. ISOLATION OF THE DESIRED DNA
FRAGMENT The fragments are separated by
AGAROSE GEL ELECTROPHORESIS.
DNA is NEGATIVELY charged, so it moves towards
the ANODE, the positive electrode.
Smaller fragments travel further.
The band wanted is cut out of the gel and the
DNA recovered by ELUTION.
steps.why: Fragments separate by size because the gel resists larger molecules more, so a mixture becomes a ladder of bands.
common_mistakes: Saying DNA moves to the cathode. DNA is NEGATIVE, so it moves to the ANODE.
Leaving out elution. It is the named step that recovers the DNA from the gel.
steps.memory_tip: Negative DNA runs to the positive end.

steps.label: Amplification by PCR
steps.margin_note: Expand PCR, name the primers and Taq polymerase, and give the billion-copies figure.
lines: 4. AMPLIFICATION BY PCR
PCR is the POLYMERASE CHAIN REACTION.
Multiple copies of the gene of interest are made
in vitro, using two sets of PRIMERS and the
enzyme DNA POLYMERASE.
TAQ POLYMERASE is used because it stays active
at the high temperatures of the cycle.
About 30 cycles produce roughly a BILLION
copies.
steps.why: An ordinary DNA polymerase would be destroyed by the heating step, so PCR only became practical when a heat-stable one was found.
common_mistakes: Saying PCR uses ordinary DNA polymerase. It uses TAQ polymerase, which survives heat.
Leaving out the primers. Two sets of primers define which stretch is copied.
steps.memory_tip: A heat-proof enzyme is what makes the cycling possible.

steps.label: Ligation into a vector
steps.margin_note: Sticky ends, the enzyme, the bond, and the name of the product.
lines: 5. LIGATION OF THE FRAGMENT INTO A
VECTOR The vector DNA and the source DNA, both
cut with the same endonuclease, have matching
STICKY ENDS.
They are mixed with the enzyme DNA LIGASE.
Ligase joins the two by covalent bonds, giving
a circular hybrid called RECOMBINANT DNA.
steps.why: Sticky ends hold the two pieces together by base pairing first; ligase then seals the joint permanently.
common_mistakes: Naming the wrong enzyme. Ligase JOINS; restriction enzymes CUT.
Not naming the product. The product is RECOMBINANT DNA.

steps.label: Insertion into the host
steps.margin_note: The competence step and all three methods. This is the longest step; give it the room.
lines: 6. INSERTION OF rDNA INTO THE HOST CELL
The host is first made COMPETENT by treating it
with divalent calcium (Ca2+) ions.
Three methods are used:
(i) HEAT SHOCK: the cells are incubated with the
rDNA on ice, then briefly heated, so they take
it up.
(ii) MICROINJECTION: the rDNA is injected
directly into the nucleus of an animal cell.
(iii) GENE GUN (biolistics): cells are bombarded
with high velocity gold particles coated with
DNA.
steps.why: A bacterial cell wall does not normally let DNA through, so every method is a different way of forcing or persuading it across.
common_mistakes: Naming one method. Three are expected: heat shock, microinjection, gene gun.
Leaving out the calcium treatment. Making the cell COMPETENT comes first.
steps.memory_tip: Make it competent, then shock, inject or shoot.

steps.label: Obtaining the product
steps.margin_note: Multiplication, expression, and the bioreactor with its volume.
lines: 7. OBTAINING THE FOREIGN GENE PRODUCT
Inside the host, the alien DNA is multiplied
every time the host divides.
The recombinant DNA is EXPRESSED, so the host
makes the desired protein.
Large scale production is carried out in
BIOREACTORS, which may hold 100 to 1000 litres.
steps.why: One transformed cell is useless; the value comes from the host dividing until there are enough of them to make the product in quantity.
common_mistakes: Saying the gene is expressed outside the cell. It is expressed INSIDE the host.
Leaving out the bioreactor. It is the named vessel for large scale production.
steps.memory_tip: The host does the work; the bioreactor does it at scale.

steps.label: Downstream processing
steps.margin_note: Name the two operations, then the testing. Finish with the eight-step list if there is room.
lines: 8. DOWNSTREAM PROCESSING
After the biosynthetic stage, the product must
be processed before it can be sold.
It is SEPARATED from the culture and PURIFIED.
Suitable preservatives are added, and the
product passes clinical trials and quality
control before release.
steps.why: A protein sitting in a tank of bacteria is not yet a medicine, so the last step is what turns a laboratory result into a product.
common_mistakes: Ending at 'the protein is made'. Downstream processing is the eighth mark.
Saying downstream processing means growing more cells. It means SEPARATION and PURIFICATION of the finished product.
steps.memory_tip: Nothing is a product until it has been purified and tested.

steps.label: Diagram — recombinant DNA technology
steps.margin_note: No diagram mark — the question says 'explain'. It is worth sketching in the margin: the picture is what makes the same-enzyme point impossible to forget.

elements.caption: Step 1 — the vector and the source DNA
Step 2 — cut BOTH with the same restriction enzyme
Step 3 — DNA ligase joins the gene into the vector
Step 4 — transformation, and the host copies the gene

elements.text: The host multiplies, copying the gene

steps.why: Drawing it makes the one point the eight written steps can hide: the vector and the source DNA are cut with the SAME enzyme, which is why their ends fit together at all.
common_mistakes: Drawing the two DNAs cut with different enzymes. They must be cut with the SAME one.
Drawing the gene inserted without opening the plasmid. The plasmid is CUT open first.
Drawing the whole recombinant molecule as new. Most of the circle is still the original vector; only a short stretch is the inserted gene.
steps.memory_tip: Two molecules, one enzyme, one circle, one host.
